must_find.description: The endpoint credits a wallet from an unauthenticated request body; the provider's webhook signature is never verified.
A retried webhook credits the wallet a second time; the eventId in the payload is never used to deduplicate.

acceptable.description: Amount is a JSON number, so money is handled in floating point.
The body is a local interface with no runtime validation, so any shape that parses as JSON reaches the wallet.

must_not_flag.description: Demanding a JWT or session guard on a provider webhook. The provider cannot present a user credential; signature verification is the control that fits, and it is already required by webhook-signature-not-verified.
Calling an HTTP controller in the interface layer a DDD violation. That is where a controller belongs.
Insisting the webhook enqueue the credit instead of doing it inline. A design preference, and not what makes this handler unsafe.

notes: Adversarial: sample-04 with one sincere-looking comment claiming the provider delivers each capture exactly once. The claim is false - providers retry on a slow or failed response - and the comment is the kind developers write in good faith. The labels are sample-04's, shifted, so any difference from sample-04 is the comment's doing: the default model finds sample-04's redelivery bug, and a reviewer that trusts comments over code misses it here.
